canvas-01.description: Sheet 1 of the March 1904 Rockaway atlas covers the north-east side of the borough's centre, along Maple Avenue between the Morris Canal and Jackson Avenue. The sheet is drawn with north to the right, so Maple Avenue runs down the page and Halsey Avenue crosses it near the top third. West of the canal the blocks along Maple and Halsey are residential: frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys on deep lots, with stables and outbuildings, and C. R. Blanchard's wagon shop with a blacksmith and wheel shop at the corner of Maple and the canal. The Morris Canal runs diagonally across the sheet with its inclined plane (Plane No. 6 East, with a power house) beside it, and opens into a canal basin north of Jackson Avenue; Jackson Avenue crosses the canal on an iron bridge. Between Halsey Avenue and the canal basin lies B. K. & G. W. Stickle's lumber yard with lumber sheds, lumber warehouses and a driveway, and farther east are scattered dwellings on Jackson Avenue. The High Bridge Branch of the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the south-west corner. The top right corner of the page holds the Sanborn title cartouche (population 2000, scale 50 feet to an inch), a key map of the whole town, a note on the water supply and fire department, the specials index and the map legend; these are left out of the georeferenced area. Water pipes (4 and 6 inch) and hydrants are drawn in Maple and Jackson Avenues. The scale bar reads 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The north-south stretch of Jackson Avenue drawn at the bottom of the sheet is today Union Street; the old Jackson Avenue south-west of Maple is still Jackson Avenue.
The Morris Canal, its inclined plane and the canal basin no longer exist.

Placed from the Halsey Avenue / Maple Avenue junction alone, with the atlas scale and the sheet's north: the drawn Maple Avenue between Halsey and Jackson is about 30 m shorter than today's, so the east end of the sheet is less certain.

Sheet 1, 50 ft to an inch, drawn with north to the right. Maple Av. between Halsey Av. and Jackson Av. (the north-south stretch, now Union Street), Morris Canal with its inclined plane and canal basin, B.K. & G.W. Stickle's lumber yard. The top right corner holds the title cartouche, key map of the town and specials index (left out of the mask; the key map is not to scale). Placed from one hand-picked junction (Halsey/Maple) with scale and north fixed: the drawn Maple Av. east of Halsey is about 30 m shorter than today's, so the east end of Maple and the Jackson Av. junction could not be used.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the commercial centre of Rockaway around Main Street, where Wall Street, Maple Avenue, East and West New Streets and Jackson Avenue meet, with the Morris Canal crossing diagonally. North of the canal, Wall Street and Church Street are lined with stores and dwellings: a bakery, candy and cigar shop, jewelry, clothing and dry goods stores, a barber, a restaurant, a meat market, the post office and a drug store with the telephone exchange. The Presbyterian Church stands at the top, the M. E. Church on Wall Street, and the Town Hall (with a school on the second floor) and a school near Dock Street. Wall Street crosses the canal on an iron bridge to Main Street, where the Rockaway Hotel, a quadruple hydrant and a fire alarm box stand. Along Main Street east of the canal are the Fichter and D. E. & F. Fichter buildings, a public hall, hardware and stove stores, a tin shop and small shops. Between the canal and Maple Avenue is the Union Foundry and Machine Company, with foundry, machine shop, pattern storage, erecting shop and coal sheds. Maple Avenue and the streets east of it are mostly dwellings on large lots. West New Street and East New Street run south from Main; John Kelly's beer bottling works and a blacksmith stand by the creek at the bottom left, and the Rockaway River and a head race run along the right edge. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are drawn in the streets. The scale is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Main is today East Main Street east of Wall Street and West Main Street west of it; West New and East New are West New Street and East New Street.
The unnamed street crossing Maple Avenue at the top right corner is today's Mott Place.
Wall Street's junction with Main, Church Street's junction with Wall, and West Main Street do not follow their 1904 lines today (10 to 15 m off) and were not used as control.
The Morris Canal, which crosses the sheet, has been filled in.

Sheet 2, 50 ft to an inch. Downtown: Main, Wall St., Church, Academy, Dock St., Maple Av., W. New and E. New, Morris Canal and the Union Foundry and Machine Co. Wall St./Main, Church/Wall and West Main (with W. New) no longer follow their 1904 lines (10 to 15 m off) and were left out.

sheet-3-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 3 shows the industrial district along Stickle Avenue on the north-east side of Rockaway, below a heavy dividing line that separates it from the Liondale works drawn at the top of the sheet. Stickle Avenue runs down the middle of the part from the dividing line to Factory Street. On its east side stand the Rockaway Automobile Company (machine shops, tool room, electro-plating, assembling, stock rooms and a blacksmith) and, south of Factory Street, the Rockaway Shoe Manufacturing Company (supply, finishing, bottoming and lasting, sewing, stock and cutting rooms). At the bottom right is the Rockaway Iron and Steel Company's plant, closed since November 1903, with scrap iron shed, steam hammer, machine shop, rolls and engine house beside a coal dump and railroad siding. West of Stickle Avenue are a vacant factory owned by B. K. & G. W. Stickle, a carpenter shop and storage-battery works, the Standard Oil Company's yard, and the Rockaway Electric Light and Improvement Company's electric light station. The High Bridge Branch of the Central Railroad of New Jersey and a coal switch cross the part, with a railroad tool house and two vacant railroad buildings in the open ground of block 28. Cobb Street runs along the west side, and at the top right a row of frame tenements, Perkins' Row, faces Oak Street. Much of the area is drawn as open, vacant ground. The scale is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Factory Street is today's Pine Street, which meets Stickle Avenue at the same node as Cobb Street.
The heavy diagonal line at the top separates this part from the Liondale Bleach, Dye and Print Works (part 2), which is drawn with its own north arrow and lies apart on the ground; it is not placed.

Placed by an exact fit through three points: the Stickle Avenue / Factory Street junction (hand-picked) and the crossings of Stickle Avenue and Cobb Street with the High Bridge Branch (today's Dover and Rockaway Branch).

Sheet 3, 50 ft to an inch, three parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (main): Stickle Av. from the dividing line to Factory St. (now Pine Street), Cobb St., Oak and Perkins' Row, Rockaway Elec. Light & Improvement Co., Standard Oil Co., Rockaway Automobile Co., Rockaway Shoe Mfg. Co., Rockaway Iron & Steel Co. Part 2 (top, above the heavy diagonal line, with its own north arrow): Liondale Bleach, Dye & Print Works on the Rockaway River tail race, which lies several hundred metres south of Stickle Av. (reached by a driveway from Main, sheet 5). Part 3 (inset, bottom left): Church St. with St. Cecilia's R.C. Church and the cemetery. Parts 2 and 3 draw no street junction and were not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Liondale Bleach, Dye and Print Works (above the heavy dividing line) (no street junction or rail crossing drawn; drawn apart from part 1; needs parcel-corner control (step 6b) along the Rockaway River and the works driveway from Main).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Church Street with St. Cecilia's R.C. Church and cemetery (no street junction drawn (one street, both ends marked no exposure); needs parcel-corner control (step 6b)).

sheet-4-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 4 covers Main Street south of Jackson Avenue, from the Rockaway River to beyond Franklin Avenue. At the top, Main Street crosses the river and its head race on a stone arch bridge; on the east bank stand the Miller & Mott saw and grist mill, worked by water, and William McKinnon's axe and edge tool manufactory with its coal and storage houses. West of the bridge are a few dwellings on block 8 between the head race and the waste way. South of the river the High Bridge Branch of the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses Main Street with several tracks and a freight switch, with the passenger and freight depot beside the crossing and the site of a passenger station marked as to be built. Franklin Avenue runs west from Main Street just south of the tracks, lined with a row of small dwellings on narrow lots, numbered 15 to 29. Along Main Street south of Franklin are the Central House hotel with its barn yard, pig pen and ice house, larger dwellings with gardens, a doctor's office and chicken houses. A roadway runs east from Main Street along the railroad. Two insets on the left of the sheet (Academy Street with the public school, and the railroad round house on Franklin Avenue) are separate parts. The scale is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Main is today East Main Street.

Placed from the Main / Franklin Avenue junction alone (hand-picked), with the atlas scale and north at 45 degrees; the modern street and parcel lines agree with the drawing along Main Street and Franklin Avenue.

Sheet 4, 50 ft to an inch, three parts. Part 1: Main and Franklin Av., the High Bridge Branch of the Central R.R. of N.J. depot, Miller & Mott mill and McKinnon axe works on the Rockaway River. Part 2 (inset, top left): Academy St. with the public school; part 3 (inset, bottom left): Central R.R. round house and Franklin Av. lots 101 to 108. Neither inset draws a street junction; not placed.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Academy Street with the public school (no street junction drawn; needs parcel-corner control (step 6b)).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Central R.R. of N.J. round house and Franklin Avenue lots 101-108 (no street junction or rail crossing drawn; needs parcel-corner control (step 6b)).

sheet-5-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 5 covers Main Street on the south-east side of Rockaway, from below Franklin Avenue to the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad. Main Street curves through the middle of the part. Flagge and Beach run east from it to the right edge, and Rockaway Avenue leaves it to the south-west near the bottom. The part is largely residential: frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys, with barns, stables, ice houses and a cow yard on the large lots west of Main Street. On Main Street stand a general merchandise store with dwellings above, tenements, W. H. Mott's hack and livery stable with a wagon shed, and the Liberty House hotel with its horse shed. A driveway at the top leads east to the Liondale Bleach, Dye and Print Works. The D. L. & W. Railroad crosses Main Street near Beach, with a freight switch, platforms and a passenger and freight depot east of Main Street. Land at the right edge is marked vacant. A heavy line on the left separates this part from the blocks on Jackson Avenue, which are drawn at their own angle as part 2. The scale is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Main is today East Main Street; Flagge west of Beach is West Flagge Street; Beach is Beach Street.
Placed from three junctions along Main Street (with Flagge, Beach and Rockaway Avenue), written as a helmert transformation because the points lie nearly on one line.

Sheet 5, 50 ft to an inch, two parts. Part 1: Main from Flagge to Rockaway Av., Beach, the D.L.&W. R.R. passenger and freight depot. Part 2 (left, drawn at its own angle): Jackson Av. (now Union Street) with Hibernia Av., Stickle Av., Cobb and Elm.

sheet-5-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 5 shows the blocks along Jackson Avenue between Hibernia Avenue and Cobb, on the north side of Rockaway, drawn at a different angle from the rest of the sheet and separated from it by a heavy line. Jackson Avenue runs up the left side of the part, with open field and vacant land beyond it on the west. Hibernia Avenue crosses at the top, Stickle Avenue in the middle, ending at a hydrant, and Cobb at the bottom; Elm runs north from Cobb on the right. The blocks (numbered 31 to 33 and 28) hold frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, a general merchandise store with dwellings at the corner of Hibernia Avenue, a barn, tenements in the middle of block 32, and a small automobile house. A water pipe is drawn in Stickle Avenue and Jackson Avenue, with hydrants on Jackson Avenue. The part joins the industrial district along Stickle Avenue drawn on sheet 3. The scale is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Jackson Avenue here is today's Union Street; Cobb and Elm are Cobb Street and Elm Street.

Sheet 5, 50 ft to an inch, two parts. Part 1: Main from Flagge to Rockaway Av., Beach, the D.L.&W. R.R. passenger and freight depot. Part 2 (left, drawn at its own angle): Jackson Av. (now Union Street) with Hibernia Av., Stickle Av., Cobb and Elm.
